Test Case: Visit the root URL while signed out
Expected Result: Public landing page renders correctly

Test Case: Sign in and view the dashboard
Expected Result: Dashboard loads with correct content and working toolbar

Test Case: Shrink the browser window below the supported width
Expected Result: Viewport warning appears; restoring size dismisses it

Test Case: Navigate between studies and observe loading indicators
Expected Result: Spinners/loading states show during fetch and clear when done

Test Case: Force an API failure (e.g. stop network) and interact with the app
Expected Result: Error boundary or status message displays; app does not crash

Test Case: Trigger success and error alerts (save/delete actions)
Expected Result: Alerts render with correct styling and dismiss properly

Test Case: Use browser Back/Forward across app pages
Expected Result: Navigation is consistent; no broken states or stale data

Test Case: Paste a direct /study/[id] URL while signed in
Expected Result: Study loads directly with correct view

Test Case: Paste a URL for a nonexistent study id
Expected Result: Friendly not-found/error handling (no crash)

Test Case: Set preferences (panel width/zoom/view toggles) then sign out and in
Expected Result: All user preferences are restored

Test Case: Open the app in a second browser tab and make changes in one
Expected Result: Other tab reflects changes after reload without corruption

Test Case: Open a toolbar menu then click elsewhere
Expected Result: Menu closes; opening a second menu closes the first

Test Case: Open a menu and press Escape
Expected Result: Menu closes and focus returns to the trigger button

Test Case: Open any modal and press Tab repeatedly
Expected Result: Focus stays trapped within the modal

Test Case: Navigate the main toolbar with keyboard only
Expected Result: All buttons reachable and operable via keyboard

Test Case: Check visible focus indicators throughout the app
Expected Result: Focused elements always have a visible focus style

Test Case: Run core flows in Chrome / Safari / Firefox
Expected Result: Behavior is consistent; unsupported browsers show a warning if applicable

Test Case: Open a large study (multiple long passages)
Expected Result: Load and interaction remain responsive (no multi-second freezes)

Test Case: Perform a mixed session (structure edits + notes + commentary + layout) then reload
Expected Result: All work is saved; nothing lost or corrupted

Test Case: Request /api/health
Expected Result: Endpoint returns a healthy status
